arxiv-1706-04743.title: Alvis–Curtis Duality for Finite General Linear Groups and a Generalized Mullineux Involution This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on the Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups and Related Topics. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/symmetric-gro
arxiv-1706-04743.creator: Olivier DUDAS † and Nicolas JACON ‡
arxiv-1706-04743.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Olivier DUDAS † and Nicolas JACON ‡. We study the effect of Alvis–Curtis duality on the unipotent representations of GL n ​ ( q ) \mathrm{GL}_{n}(q) in non-defining characteristic ℓ \ell . We show that the permutation induced on the simple modules can be expressed in terms of a generalization of the Mullineux involution on the set of all partitions, which involves both ℓ \ell and the order of q q modulo ℓ \ell .

arxiv-2012-13302.title: Leptonic and Hadronic Radiative Processes in Supermassive-Black-Hole Jets
arxiv-2012-13302.creator: Matteo Cerruti
arxiv-2012-13302.description: Abstract Supermassive black holes lying in the center of galaxies can launch relativistic jets of plasma along their polar axis. The physics of black-hole jets is a very active research topic in astrophysics, owing to the fact that many questions remain open on the physical mechanisms of jet launching, of particle acceleration in the jet, and on the radiative processes.

arxiv-2111-03385.title: A monotonicity result for the first Steklov-Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalue
arxiv-2111-03385.creator: Nunzia Gavitone, Gianpaolo Piscitelli
arxiv-2111-03385.description: Abstract . In this paper, we consider the first Steklov-Dirichlet eigenvalue of the Laplace operator in annular domains with a spherical hole. We prove a monotoni- city result with respect to the hole, when the outer region is centrally symmetric. MSC 2020: Primary: 35J25, 35P15; Secondary: 28A75, 49Q10. Keywords : Laplacian eigenvalue, Steklov-Dirichlet boundary conditions, Shape derivative. 1.

arxiv-2207-01767.title: Three approaches to chiral form interactions
arxiv-2207-01767.creator: Oleg Evnin
arxiv-2207-01767.description: Abstract Imperial-TP-KM-2022-4 ABSTRACT We briefly review and critically compare three approaches to constructing Lagrangian theories of self-interacting Abelian chiral form fields with manifest Lorentz invariance. The first approach relies on the original ideas of Pasti, Sorokin, and Tonin (PST) and has been explored since the late 1990s. The second approach was introduced by Ashoke Sen in 2015.

arxiv-2208-08499.title: Every graph is eventually Turán-good
arxiv-2208-08499.creator: Natasha Morrison, JD Nir, Sergey Norin, Paweł Rzążewski, Alexandra Wesolek
arxiv-2208-08499.description: Abstract Let H H be a graph. We show that if r r is large enough as a function of H H , then the r r -partite Turán graph maximizes the number of copies of H H among all K r + 1 K_{r+1} -free graphs on a given number of vertices.

arxiv-2211-01472.title: The Need for Medically Aware Video Compression in Gastroenterology
arxiv-2211-01472.creator: Joel ShorVerily Life Sciencesjoelshor@verily.com, Nick JohnstonGoogle Researchnickj@google.com
arxiv-2211-01472.description: Abstract Compression is essential to storing and transmitting medical videos, but the effect of compression on downstream medical tasks is often ignored. Furthermore, systems in practice rely on standard video codecs, which naively allocate bits between medically relevant frames or parts of frames.

arxiv-2310-17808.title: A Novel Fast Path Planning Approach for Mobile Devices using Hybrid Quantum Ant Colony Optimization Algorithm
arxiv-2310-17808.creator: Mayukh Sarkar 1 , Jitesh Pradhan 1 , Anil Kumar Singh 2 , Hathiram Nenavath 3
arxiv-2310-17808.description: Abstract With IoT systems’ increasing scale and complexity, maintenance of a large number of nodes using stationary devices is becoming increasingly difficult. Hence, mobile devices are being employed that can traverse through a set of target locations and provide the necessary services.

arxiv-2502-06672.title: Efficient Spatial Estimation of Perceptual Thresholds for Retinal Implants via Gaussian Process Regression Thanks: 1 RS and MB are with the Department of Computer Science, University of California, Santa Barbara, CA 93106, USA. Thanks: 2 MB is with the Department of Psychological & Brain Sciences, U
arxiv-2502-06672.creator: Roksana Sadeghi, Michael Beyeler
arxiv-2502-06672.description: Abstract Retinal prostheses restore vision by electrically stimulating surviving neurons, but calibrating perceptual thresholds (i.e., the minimum stimulus intensity required for perception) remains a time-intensive challenge, especially for high-electrode-count devices. Since neighboring electrodes exhibit spatial correlations, we propose a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) framework to predict thresholds at unsampled locations while leveraging uncertainty estimates to guide adaptive sampling.

arxiv-2508-11968.title: Dynamical quark mass and finite volume effects in the Dyson-Schwinger Equations
arxiv-2508-11968.creator: Li-Juan Zhou, De-Xian Wei, Zhong-Yi Liu, Hong-Wei Zhong
arxiv-2508-11968.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Li-Juan Zhou, De-Xian Wei, Zhong-Yi Liu, Hong-Wei Zhong. Within the framework of Dyson-Schwinger equations(DSEs) and by means of the Multiple Reflection Expansion approximation, we study the finite volume effects of the constituent quark mass in a strong external magnetic field. Since the magnetic field has influence on the coupling constant, the coupling constant controls the strength of strongly interaction in QCD, so we adopt the magnetic-field-dependent running coupling constant in simulation.

arxiv-2510-01768.title: Dimers for Relativistic Toda Models with Reflective Boundaries
arxiv-2510-01768.creator: Kimyeong Lee, and Norton Lee
arxiv-2510-01768.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kimyeong Lee, and Norton Lee. We construct dimer graphs for relativistic Toda chains associated with classical untwisted Lie algebras of A, B, C 0 , C π , D types and twisted A, D types. We show that the Seiberg-Witten curve of 5d 𝒩 = 1 \mathcal{N}=1 pure supersymmetric gauge theory of gauge group G G is a spectral curve of the relativistic Toda chain of the dual group G ∨ G^{\vee} .

arxiv-2511-16440.title: StreetView-Waste: A Multi-Task Dataset for Urban Waste Management
arxiv-2511-16440.creator: Diogo J. Paulo, João Martins, Hugo Proença, João C. Neves, [4pt] University of Beira Interior, Portugal
arxiv-2511-16440.description: Abstract Urban waste management remains a critical challenge for the development of smart cities. Despite the growing number of litter detection datasets, the problem of monitoring overflowing waste containers — particularly from images captured by garbage trucks — has received little attention.

arxiv-2602-02697.title: Degeneracies and modelling choices in double-plane time-delay cosmography
arxiv-2602-02697.creator: Daniel Johnson ,, Pierre Fleury, Martin Millon
arxiv-2602-02697.description: Abstract Double-plane gravitational lensing is a rare but increasingly observed phenomenon in which the light from a distant source is lensed by two foreground objects at different redshifts. Such systems can be used to provide simultaneous constraints on the Hubble constant H 0 H_{0} and the dark-energy equation of state, independent of and complementary to other probes.

pmc-11556885.title: Relationship between systolic blood pressure and renal function on clinical outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation: a report from the prospective AF-GEN-UK Registry
pmc-11556885.creator: Alena Shantsila, Gregory Y.H. Lip, Deirdre A. Lane
pmc-11556885.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background:Blood pressure (BP) extremes and renal (dys)function contribute to poor outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). pmc-11709371.title: The anti‐platelet agent prasugrel reverses the cerebral blood flow deficit and memory impairment induced by hypertension in ApoE4‐positive mice
pmc-11709371.creator: Lianne J Trigiani, Nicole E Chernavsky, Rachel Kim, Robert F Hawkins, Nuri Hong, Keri Yamaguchi, Jonah Bernard, Amanda Huang, Gina H Bae, Daniel A Rivera, Nathaniel Allan‐Rahill, Michael Lamont, Costantino Iadecola, Nozomi Nishimura, Chris B Schaffer
pmc-11709371.description: BackgroundSeveral genetic and cardiovascular risk factors increase incidence of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD). Hypertension and the ε4 allele of apolipoprotein E (ApoE) are powerful drivers of cognitive impairment in ADRD. These risk factors are also associated with decreased cerebral blood flow (CBF).

pmc-11756362.title: A safe and effective treatment for refractory malignant ascites: the use of pigtail catheters
pmc-11756362.creator: Akif Doğan, Ömer Aydıner
pmc-11756362.description: PurposeRecurrent malignant ascites is a common and challenging condition in cancer patients, often lacking a standardized treatment protocol. Small-scale studies in the literature have been insufficient to establish a treatment standard. The aim of our study was to investigate the effectiveness and safety of pigtail peritoneal catheter application in the treatment of malignant ascites.

pmc-11891137.title: Etiology and Antimicrobial Resistance of Culture-Positive Infections in Ugandan Infants: A Cohort Study of 7000 Neonates and Infants
pmc-11891137.creator: Hannah G Davies, Mary Kyohere, Valerie Tusubira, Alexander Amone, Amusa Wamawobe, Cleophas Komugisha, Philippa Musoke, Lauren Hookham, Pooja Ravji, Melanie Etti, Juliet Nsimire Sendagala, Dan R Shelley, Caitlin Farley, Merryn Voysey, Owen B Spiller, Joseph Peacock, Musa Sekikubo, Paul T Heath, Kirst
pmc-11891137.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundEpidemiological evidence about the etiology and antimicrobial resistance of neonatal infections remains limited in low-resource settings. We aimed to describe the etiology of neonatal infections in a prospective observational cohort study conducted at two hospital sites in Kampala, Uganda.MethodsBabies admitted to either unit with risk factors or signs of sepsis, pneumonia, or meningitis had a blood culture, nasopharyngeal swab, and lumbar puncture (if indicated) collected. Basic demographics were collected, and babies were followed up until discharge or death to determine admission outcome.

pmc-12559432.title: DNA methylation patterns facilitate tracing the origin of neuroendocrine neoplasms
pmc-12559432.creator: Benjamin Goeppert, Alphonse Charbel, Reka Toth, Yue Zhang, Danial Tabbakh, Thomas Albrecht, Daniel Schrimpf, Louis de Mestier, Jérôme Cros, Monika Nadja Vogel, De-Hua Chang, Eva-Marie Bohn, Alexander Brobeil, Junfang Ji, Stephan Singer, Petr V Nazarov, Aurel Perren, Leonidas Apostolidis, Andreas von
pmc-12559432.description: Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NEN) are thought to originate from diffuse neuroendocrine networks and therefore most frequently arise in the gastrointestinal tract and lungs. The liver is a frequent site of metastasis of NEN but also the existence of primary hepatic NEN has been proposed.

pmc-12702416.title: Nature’s chemical computer: Herbal residue-derived carbon dots build logic gates for H2O2 tracking and ecological antimicrobials
pmc-12702416.creator: Xiangru Hou, Denggerile Ao, Lu Ga, Gang Dai, Jun Ai
pmc-12702416.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In this work, we report the use of logic platforms and iron-doped carbon dots (Fe-CDs) as a promising peroxidase-like analogue for the qualitative quantification of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). The synthesised Fe-CDs exhibited excellent peroxidase-like (POD-like) activity compared to carbon dots (CDs), which catalyzed the formation of blue oxidation product (ox-TMB) with maximum absorption at 652 nm from the chromogenic substrate 3,3′, 5,5′ - tetramethylbenzidine (TMB). Steady state kinetic analysis shows that Fe-CDs have strong POD-like activity.

pmc-13490424.creator: Jillian L King, Devin P Effinger, Cameron Basquez-Pfeifer, Janae R Wallingford, Joselynn R Calderon, Caden K O’Connell, Scott M Thompson

pmc-13516160.title: Semaglutide Exposure During Pregnancy: Results from the FAERS Database
pmc-13516160.creator: Alessia Zinzi, Mario Gaio, Annamaria Mascolo, Gorizio Pieretti, Mattia Cipriani, Joao Marcos Della Ragione, Rossana D’Amato, Francesco Rossi, Annalisa Capuano, Rosanna Ruggiero
pmc-13516160.description: Background/Objectives: The increased incidence of obesity and type 2 diabetes, along with the growing use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), particularly semaglutide, among women of childbearing age makes it especially important to assess their safety profile during pregnancy. Methods: A post-marketing study was conducted using reports from the U.S. FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database (2017–2025).
